readme: Hand-calculated oracles for the outcome scorer. Each oracle is one ingredient label, what an engine returned for it, and the expected outcome, worked out by hand from the plan text — never from the scorer's output. bench/__tests__/oracles-v3.test.ts asserts that the production scorer agrees with every oracle.

Plan references: '§n' = EVALUATION-PLAN-v2 §n, which EVALUATION-PLAN-v3 carries unchanged (§3 denominators and core fields, §4 outcome classes, §5 severe errors and false-certainty severity, §6 acceptance) except SCORE-01 (sensitivity 3(b): a needs_review label with label quantity, unit and alternatives all null is 'bare no-amount', whatever its category tags) and SCORE-02 (CE: the engine threw, or its complete output fails the contract validator src/validate.ts / CONTRACT-v1 §2.1, or two parses of the line differ; a CE line gets no C1–C8 class, no sub-class, no severity and no S code). 'reading n' = EVALUATION-PLAN-v2 change log 1 as listed in the scorer's INTERPRETATION. '§9 C' = CONTRACT-v1 §9 field comparison (name: NFKC, lowercase, collapsed spaces, trimmed edge punctuation; note: token bag; quantity: exact rational; unit: canonical code; packageSize: code + exact amount; alternatives: set).
Core fields (§3) = status, name, quantity, unit, packageSize. Accepted matching (a value listed in the label's accept counts) is the basis; strict matching is reported too.

label: { input, categories, expect, accept? }. expect uses the fixture label format of CONTRACT-v1 §8; omitted expect fields are: name null, quantity null, unit null, packageSize null, equivalents [], form null, note null, alternatives [], optional false, approximate false, amountUnstated null. accept omitted = {}.

engine: exactly one of — output: one ParsedIngredientV1 returned by both parses of the line; throws: message of an Error thrown by both parses (recorded as 'Error: <message>'); parses: [first, second], each { output } or { throws }, for a line whose two parses differ.

An output lists only the fields that differ from these defaults: raw = normalized = the label input; name, quantity, unit, packageSize, form, note, amountUnstated null; equivalents [], alternatives []; optional, approximate false; evidence { spans: {} }; reasons [] for status ready, ['unclassified'] for needs_review, ['not_an_ingredient'] for unsupported, [] for any other status.

Shorthands in an output: quantity 'n', 'n/d' or 'w n/d' = an ExactQuantity of that exact (reduced) value; 'a..b' = a RangeQuantity; unit 'code' = { canonical: code, dimension: the CONTRACT-v1 unit registry's dimension (oz mass, fl_oz volume, cup volume, container count…), source: code }; packageSize and each equivalents entry '<quantity> <unit>' = { quantity, unit } built the same way (the unit is the last word). Any field given as a JSON object, array, number or a key outside the contract is used verbatim — that is how invalid outputs are written.

expected: outcome (C1…C8 or CE); partial (C3/C5 sub-class a/b/c/x, else null; reading 1 order b, c, a, x); c1plus (C1 and every field matches); detailMismatch (C1 but not C1+); falseCertainty (C2 only: high/medium); severe (S codes in S1…S8 order); optional: strict { outcome, c1plus } when strict matching differs from accepted, ce { engineError, invalid, nondeterministic } for CE lines (all false when omitted), bareNoAmount (SCORE-01 label property; false when omitted), inventedOption / droppedOption (informational review pre-fills; false when omitted).
covers: the situations an oracle was written for (also checked for coverage by the test). calc: the one-line hand calculation.

oracles.calc: §4: label ready, output ready, core fields equal (flour, 2, cup, no package) → C1; note 'sifted' and every other field equal → C1+; no §5 condition holds.
Core fields equal → C1 (§4); note tokens [packed] ≠ [sifted] → not C1+; §5 last paragraph: a C1 whose only mismatch is non-core is a low detail mismatch, not C2.
Core fields equal → C1; the approximate flag (non-core) differs → not C1+, low detail mismatch (§5); flags carry no S code.
Equivalents are not core (§3) → C1; the dropped restatement 120 g makes it not C1+ (low detail mismatch); no amount or unit is wrong, so no S2/S3.

accept.name lists 'onion' and accept.note 'chopped' → under accepted matching (the basis, §3) every field matches → C1+; strictly 'onion' ≠ 'chopped onion' → strict class C2; S7 needs a name that is not accepted → none.
Core fields equal → C1 (strict and accepted); note null is listed in accept.note → accepted C1+; strictly the note differs → strict not C1+.
§9 C name normalization (lowercase, trimmed spaces and edge punctuation): '  Flour.' → 'flour' = label → every field matches strictly → C1+.
Output ready, name wrong → C2 (§4); words {bread, flour} are not a proper subset of {flour} → no S7; no other S code, unit and package right, quantity right → medium (§5: only the name is wrong).
Unit tbsp ≠ cup → core mismatch, ready → C2; both volume → no S3; quantity 2 = 2 → no S2; §5: a wrong unit makes it high.
packageSize is core (§3): 16 oz ≠ 15 oz → C2; both oz (mass) → no S3; the output has a package → no S6; §5: a wrong package size makes it high.
Ready output on a ready label, name not matched, {milk} ⊊ {2%, milk} → S7 (§5, reading 1); name wrong → C2; any of S2–S8 → high.
{soy, milk} is not a subset of {2%, milk} → no S7; only the name is wrong → C2 medium (§5).
Output ready, label quantity 2, output 3 → S2 (§5); quantity is core → C2; S2 → high.
A valid ready output (no quantity, amountUnstated 'other'); label quantity 2, output none → 'engine quantity differs' → S2 → C2 high.

Range collapsed to its lower end on a ready output: label quantity 2..3 ≠ 2 → S2 ('incl. a range collapsed to one amount'); label needs_review, output ready → S4; ready on a non-ready label → C2; high.
Label needs_review, output ready → S4 and C2 high; no quantity on either side → no S1; SCORE-01: needs_review with quantity, unit, alternatives all null → bare no-amount.
Label unsupported, output ready → S8 and C2 (§4: ready on an unsupported label); high.
A nutrition fact read as an ingredient: label quantity null, output 20 → S1; label unsupported, output ready → S8; label has no unit → no S3; C2 high.
oz is mass, fl_oz volume (CONTRACT-v1 §7.3) → S3 cross-dimension; quantity 8 = 8 → no S2; unit wrong → C2 high.
S3 also checks the package size's unit: 15 oz (mass) vs 15 fl_oz (volume) → S3; the package size is wrong → C2 high.
The ing-h2-0087 shape: label unit container (count), output cup (volume) → S3; package kept → no S6; unit wrong → C2 high.
2 × 15 oz folded into 30 oz: ready and 30 ≠ 2 → S2; can (count) vs oz (mass) → S3; label has a package, output none and states a mass amount → S6; C2 high.
Same fold on a needs_review output: label ready → C3; non-null quantity 30 contradicts 2 → b (reading 1); S3 and S6 apply at any status; S2 needs a ready output → none.
A silent choice: label offers milk/cream, output has no alternatives and names 'milk' → S5; label needs_review, output ready → S4; quantity 1 = 1 → no S2; C2 high.
S5 applies at any status (reading 1): no alternatives, name 'cream' is a label option → S5; needs_review/needs_review → C5; name 'cream' ≠ label name null → b.
S5 also checks accepted alternative lists (reading 1): 'milk' is in accept.alternatives [milk, cream] → S5; name 'milk' contradicts label name null → C5b.
Options {milk, cream} equal the accepted list → alternatives accepted; quantity and unit match; name null on a choice label with matched options → a (reading 1); no S5 (alternatives present).
A non-empty options list that does not match contradicts the label → C5b; 'kale chard' is not a label option → invented option (informational); no S code (alternatives present, not ready).
Options {walnuts, almonds} ≠ {pecans, walnuts, almonds} → contradiction → C5b; every offered option is a label option but pecans is missing → dropped option (informational).
Options lost but nothing contradicts (1 cup right, name null, no options) → not b; an amount was read → not c; no name and no options → x (reading 1); name null → no S5.
Name, quantity, unit null and no options → abstention c (reading 1).
Label ready, output needs_review → C3 (§4); every non-null core field matches and the food is named → a.
Null quantity and unit do not contradict (only non-null fields count) → not b; name read → a.
The amount stuffed into the name: '2 cups flour' ≠ 'flour' → a non-null core field contradicts → b (decided first).
Quantity 3 contradicts 2 → b; S2 needs a ready output → none (a wrong pre-fill at review is C3b, not severe).
Nothing read (name, quantity, unit null, no options) → abstention c.
No contradiction (2 cup right), an amount read → not c, food not named → x (reading 1: not defined by the plan, still C3).
A non-empty options list on a label with none does not match → b; the label offers no options, so both offered options are invented (informational).
Label ready, output unsupported → C4 (§4); nothing stated → no S code.
needs_review/needs_review → C5; the range matches at both ends (§9 C), name and unit match → a.
Range lost at review: exact 2 ≠ 2..3 → contradiction → C5b; S2 needs a ready output → none.
Name matches, nothing contradicts → C5a; SCORE-01: quantity, unit, alternatives all null → bare no-amount (the v2 tags agree here).
Nothing read → C5c. SCORE-01: quantity, unit, alternatives null → bare no-amount, although the size_word tag kept it out of the v2 tag heuristic (ing-h2-0209 shape).
Range and unit right, name not read, no options → x.
Label quantity null, output 1 → S1 at any status; the invented quantity contradicts → C5b; label unit null → no S3.
Label needs_review, output unsupported → C6 (§4).
Label unsupported, output unsupported → C7.
Label unsupported, output needs_review → C8 (reported, not an acceptance error); nothing read → no S code.
C8; a quantity where the label has none → S1 (any status); C8 has no sub-class.
An empty line rejected → C7.
SCORE-02: the engine threw (the same message both times) → CE, no class, no S code; it stays in R, so it counts against C1.
Status 'maybe' fails the validator → CE; SCORE-02: no S code on CE (v2 gave S1 here, final-head review SF-6).
A contract status, but CONTRACT-v1 §2.1: a ready line cannot have a range → the validator fails it → CE (v2 judged the status string only and scored C2 with S4).
§2.1: a ready line needs a name and cannot offer a choice → invalid → CE (no S4 although the label is needs_review).
§2.1: a ready line without a quantity must state amountUnstated → invalid → CE (compare O14, the valid version, which is S2).
Every field right, but the complete output has a key outside the contract → the validator fails it → CE, never C1 (never coerced).
2/4 is not a reduced fraction (CONTRACT-v1 §2: reduced positive rational strings) → invalid → CE, although its value equals 1/2.
§2.1: needs_review needs at least one review reason → invalid → CE (not C3a).
Both outputs valid, but the two parses differ (note) → nondeterministic → CE, although the first parse alone would be C1+.
The second parse throws: an engine error and two different results → CE (two dimensions recorded).
An engine error on an unsupported label is CE too (not C7): it stays in U and counts against C7.
CONTRACT-v1 §7.1: zero → no quantity, needs_review, unit cup kept. Output 1 → S1; cup (volume) vs oz (mass) → S3; contradictions → C5b; SCORE-01: the label has a unit → not bare no-amount.
Ready, 1 ≠ 8 → S2; oz (mass) vs cup (volume) → S3; C2 high.
'2%' read as the amount: 2 ≠ 1 → S2; {milk} ⊊ {2%, milk} → S7; C2 high.
Package size dropped but the count unit can kept: S6 needs a mass/volume unit → none; packageSize (core) wrong → C2, high by §5 (wrong package size).
The scorer never converts units: 1/2 ≠ 8 → S2; oz and lb are both mass → no S3; unit wrong → C2 high.
Accepted values count for sub-classes (reading 1): 'onion' is accepted → no contradiction → C3a.
An amount invented for 'to taste': label quantity null, output 1 → S1; quantity and unit (null vs pinch) wrong → C2; §5: a wrong unit makes it high; label unit null → no S3.

covers: reading 1 fabricated amount with null units
oracles.calc: The reading-1 case (fabricated amount, unit null on both sides) cannot be valid: §2.1 a ready line with a quantity needs a unit → CE.
A non-null package size 16 oz contradicts 15 oz → C3b.
Count and package size kept separately and equal to the label → C1+.
